short: A Soviet high-speed interceptor and reconnaissance aircraft that could sustain speeds close to Mach 3.
full:
Introduced in 1970, the Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25 was designed specifically to intercept fast, high-altitude American bombers like the B-58 Hustler and the XB-70 Valkyrie. Constructed largely from heavy nickel-steel alloys to withstand the extreme heat of high-speed flight, it was powered by immense turbojet engines that allowed it to reach Mach 2.8 in operational configurations, and even faster at the risk of engine destruction. Its existence initially triggered panic in Western intelligence circles, directly spurring the development of the F-15 Eagle.

In reality, the MiG-25 was highly specialized; it possessed poor maneuverability at low altitudes and a limited combat radius. Nevertheless, its sheer speed made it a highly effective reconnaissance platform over hostile territory, seeing service in conflicts across the Middle East. It was finally retired by its last military operators in 2022.
